component.name: Westering
component.summary: A few quiet minutes under tonight's real sky

description.p: Westering is a few quiet minutes at the end of the day, to wind down and come back to what matters to you. It draws the real sky over you tonight in fine dots: the stars, the Moon at its real phase, and the planets that are really up. Find a few things, hear a story, and set down what's weighing on you, to watch it go down in the west with the turning sky. Each visit slows as you go, dims for a real reason, and ends by naming something you can go outside and see.

ul.li: The sky is worked out on your computer from your time zone: no location service
A few things to find each night, and then the sky is done until it turns
Set down what's weighing on you, and watch it set in the west
A logbook kept as plain files you can read, copy or delete, with a small chart of each evening's sky
No network access at all: nothing you write leaves your computer

description.p: While it keeps you company, a change of music or volume is said at the top of the window, where it can be seen. It was drawn at the foot, behind the wisp's moss.
An evening that carries itself along, ends on a thought that fits it, and leaves a chart of its sky in the logbook.

ul.li: The guided evening carries on by itself: put a card away, or answer what the sky asks, and the view turns to the next find
Winding down is offered about a quarter of an hour in, ends on one last thought that never repeats the evening, and settles onto one of the five calmest pieces of music
Each night's page in the logbook has a chart of that evening's sky, with what you found, drew and set down
On the night of a plan, a mark on the horizon shows where to look, or where it will rise and when
Looking back at an old weight meets every answer the same way
A photograph for everything that can be found, and the keys as a table under ?
Space always carries on, Tab says when the sky is done, and the wisp's words stay clear of tonight's list

description.p: Guided or free look, company in the background, and the ground by day.

ul.li: Every evening starts guided; once the wisp has walked the sky with you, free look lets you click anything that glows to close in on it
Keep me company: the sky rests and the music plays on in a window of any size, with a word now and then about looking after yourself
By day the view turns to the ground under a daylit sky: the real Sun, a stone's shadow, and three small things for the time of year
Winding down asks plainly, breathes with you, and only ever gets darker
The wisp listens while you write, keeps quiet while you look, and waits for you to move its words on
Over 160 more photographs of the sky, facts and lore checked against the sources, and music in four styles

description.p: Every evening shows its three parts: set it down, look up, wind down. Winding down is chosen, and ends outside or in bed.
Constellation figures from Stellarium's modern set, and hints for what's under the pointer.
Night Sky is now Westering. Your logbook comes across the first time it opens.
